scope: Chosen practical substring and search edges, with existing ASCII and character-domain checks; no new native behavior claim

implementation_choices.substring: source[start-1:start-1+min(count,254)]; positive one-based start, nonnegative INTEGER count; clip at source end; zero count and starts past end produce initialized empty STRING
implementation_choices.substring_capacity: Return at most 254 logical characters before consumption; bound the slice before allocation, including a MAXINT count; source expressions may exceed 254 characters; destination/routine result may truncate further
implementation_choices.index: Python str.find(search)+1; first exact case-sensitive match, zero when absent, one for an empty search including an empty source
implementation_choices.length_and_characters: STR_LEN counts logical ASCII characters; CHR accepts INTEGER codes 0..127; ORD requires a one-based INTEGER index inside current contents
implementation_choices.evaluation: Actuals evaluated once left to right before operation validation; immutable STRING values captured before later argument effects; evaluation errors skip later actuals
implementation_choices.failure: No destination assignment on operation error; preserve earlier effects/nested requests including argument mutations of that destination; unwind routine frames on error or ABORT
implementation_choices.report: string_operation_policy records chosen equivalents, capacity, evaluation order, failures and controller_validated=false

retained_boundaries: Initialized ASCII STRING inputs even for empty results/searches; exact INTEGER types and existing signed-32-bit expression checks
Positive one-based SUB_STR starts; nonnegative counts; CHR and ORD domains
Existing destination/result capacities, ownership, call-depth, step and FOR-counter guards
Combined rendered WRITE output <=254 characters; no native string ABI or controller runtime claim
Conservative substring/search guards remain internal for the future strict milestone
